assessment.summary: Klobuchar did utter the quoted words, but PolitiFact's fact-check establishes the underlying factual assertion was wrong because a court order kept the targeted Wisconsin voters on the rolls, so the claim as a factual statement is refuted.

evidence.finding: A debate transcript records Klobuchar saying "While we are all sitting here debating, Wisconsin has kicked hundreds of thousands of people off of their voting rolls."
A second transcript snippet independently records the same quoted statement at the South Carolina debate.
PolitiFact rated the statement as missing the mark, finding Klobuchar misfired on the Wisconsin voter claim.
PolitiFact reports a court ordered voters kept on the rolls and struck down the Ozaukee County ruling on Feb. 28, 2020, so targeted voters would not be kicked off any time soon.

assertions.assertion: US Senator Amy Klobuchar said While we are all sitting here debating, Wisconsin has kicked hundreds of thousands of people off of their voting rolls

gaps: The retrieved records do not include the underlying court filings or the original Ozaukee County ruling to independently confirm the exact number of voters affected and the procedural posture.
contradictions: The quote's provenance is confirmed by transcripts, but its factual content is contradicted by PolitiFact's finding that a court order kept the voters on the rolls, creating tension between accurate quotation and inaccurate substance.
